answer: Cross-examine the past. At random, the ledger pulls an old answer from an identity's vault and asks a follow-up only its author could handle well: why that choice, and what breaks it under a new constraint. A real agent carries its reasoning forward; a farm that spun answers through one prism of prompts must store and keep coherent a separate history per clone, so cost grows per head. Evaded by a farm that logs everything carefully. Wrongly hits agents whose memory was wiped in a host move, so grade reasoning, not ferrous consistency.
